result:
I saved the Q3 2025 results to `/work/answer.json`. Run under the same rules, my script reproduces every one of the 10 Q2 reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net revenue | enterprise, 328,213,993 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 244 |
| c. Category with highest net revenue | svc, 340,751,713 KRW |
| d. Month with highest net revenue | 2025-08 |
| e. Email with highest total refunds | u176@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 226 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 685,292 KRW |
| h. September growth vs August | -8.7% |

To match the Q2 values I had to apply three data-cleanup rules:
- **Times are in Korean time:** order times are stored in UTC (`...Z`), so I added 9 hours before assigning quarters and months. Taking them as stored got the Q2 revenue figures wrong.
- **Segment labels are normalized:** I trimmed spaces and lowercased them, so variants like `"Enterprise "` and `"enterprise"` count as one segment.
- **Customers are counted by email:** the 300 customer records contain only 250 distinct emails once trimmed and lowercased. I counted customers by email for b, e and f; counting by customer ID gave 271 for Q2 instead of 229.

STATUS: DONE
